conventions: The refrain יָבוֹא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד → the King of glory will come in keeps in with בּוֹא as part of its lexeme (come in / enter, rule 44) in both v7 and v9; the competing reading marking in added was considered and not taken. The vocatives of the same refrain are allocated by position under rule 36: O ye gates and ye everlasting doors go to the nouns, the ye of be ye lifted up (v7) to the Niphal imperative.
report: Checked all ten candidate lemmas; every difference is licensed by the ASV's own rendering and none is a split. הוּא: eleven buckets of suffix/pronoun realizations, plus the v10 resumptive הוּא left unrepresented under rule 20's tripartite reading (copula to the predicate מִי) beside the v10b הוּא that holds its own He — both are rule 20 as written.

The refrain מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד is analysed identically in v7, v8, v9 and v10b: rectum article takes the fronted the (rule 29), construct keeps King, rectum takes of glory; v10b adds the copula to the predicate construct (rule 20). In v10a the ASV writes this and no the, so the demonstrative זֶה takes this and the article is unrepresented (rule 41); in v8 the ASV writes the and no this, so the article takes the and זֶה is unrepresented. The two verses differ because the English differs, not the analysis.

מִי takes the copula in v8 and v10a as the clause's predicate (rule 20's What man is this) and only who before the finite verbs of v3. נָשָׂא, יהוה, בְּ, לְ vary only with the English written for them; v7 and v9 place the vocative ye / O ye and the imperative's ye by position exactly alike (rule 36), and both keep in with בּוֹא → come in (rule 44).

The three added units (v4 that hath, v6 italic even, v9 them) each answer to no morpheme and no verse folds the same English into a licensing word elsewhere: v4 follows rule 2's own He that hath example, v6's even stands before an appositive no marker or waw stands on (rule 16), v9's them is a supplied object with no suffix (rule 44), while v6's him and v2's it are suffixes and take their pronouns.

BSB disagreements (v8 זֶה, v10 הוּא, v10 first הַ) are all convention differences — BSB gives this/that to the demonstrative or pronoun where the ASV writes no such word, and gives the article the determiner the ASV wrote for זֶה. None is an error.

v4 s013: the projection carries the 1cs suffix (ketiv נַפְשִׁי) while the ASV writes his (qere); no variant unit is recorded for the slot, so the English is aligned as printed under rule 53's closing paragraph and noted. Nothing to change.
